findings.evidence: `pkg/executor/distsql.go:641-653` builds a `workerPool` with `MaxWorkers = max(1, e.indexLookupConcurrency)` and no extra slot for the index task; the index scan itself is executed in that same pool via `e.pool.submit(...)` (`pkg/executor/distsql.go:732-814`). Each lookup task enqueues a table task into the pool and then immediately sends the task to `resultCh` (`pkg/executor/distsql.go:1085-1097`), while the consumer blocks on `<-task.doneCh` before it can advance (`pkg/executor/distsql.go:956-965`). `resultCh` is buffered by `LookupTableTaskChannelSize` (`pkg/executor/distsql.go:619`), which defaults to 50 (`pkg/executor/distsql.go:74-75`). Concurrency can be set to 1 (`pkg/sessionctx/variable/sysvar.go:2072-2074`). With `MaxWorkers=1`, the pool cannot spawn a second worker (`pkg/executor/utils.go:134-165`).
findings.fix:
Ensure table lookups can run concurrently with the index scan even when `e.indexLookupConcurrency == 1`:
- Prefer: keep index worker as a dedicated goroutine (outside the pool) and use the pool only for table tasks (so `MaxWorkers` maps 1:1 to table concurrency, as before).
- Alternative: set pool capacity to include the index task (e.g. `MaxWorkers = e.indexLookupConcurrency + 1`) and spawn a worker as soon as there is any pending table task (don’t require `tasks > 1` / `TolerablePendingTasks=1` when the only running worker is the index task).
findings.impact: If `tidb_index_lookup_concurrency`/`tidb_executor_concurrency` is 1 and the index scan produces more than `LookupTableTaskChannelSize` lookup tasks (e.g. large scans where tasks > 50), the index task can block on `resultCh` while all table tasks are queued but cannot run (no available pool worker). The session goroutine is simultaneously blocked on `task.doneCh`, causing the query to hang indefinitely.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master` (3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd): the same pattern remains (index task runs in the same pool capped by `indexLookupConcurrency`, and table tasks are pool tasks).
findings.verify:
Minimal repro (manual): set `tidb_executor_concurrency=1` (or `tidb_index_lookup_concurrency=1`), run a query that uses IndexLookupExecutor and returns > ~1,000,000 handles (so >50 batches at 20k/batch) and confirm it can complete.
Stronger (unit/integration): temporarily set `executor.LookupTableTaskChannelSize=1` (as done in `pkg/executor/test/seqtest/seq_executor_test.go`) with concurrency=1 and ensure the query does not hang.
findings.what: Deadlock risk when index lookup concurrency is 1: the index scan runs as a task in the same worker pool whose `MaxWorkers` is also 1, so table lookup tasks can’t run until the index scan finishes. If the index scan produces more than the `resultCh` buffer (default 50) it blocks on `resultCh` while `Next()` is blocked on `task.doneCh`, causing an indefinite hang.

subject: executor: run idxlookup workers in a pool (#58033)
summary: The commit replaces idxlookup’s dedicated table-worker goroutines with a per-executor `workerPool` and runs the index scan inside that pool. This introduces a real deadlock when `tidb_index_lookup_concurrency`/`tidb_executor_concurrency` is set to 1 and the scan yields more than the `resultCh` buffer worth of tasks (default 50); the issue remains present on `upstream/master`.
